problem: The numbers in the Celsius trap are wrong twice over. Putting 250 °C and 300 °C straight into T_C/(T_H − T_C) gives 250/50 = 5, not 5.26, and the correct Carnot COP for those two Celsius temperatures is 523/50 ≈ 10.5, not 5. So the trap as written teaches a false arithmetic and a false reference answer.
fix: Use a case where the error is visible: cold space at −23 °C (250 K) and surroundings at 27 °C (300 K). The correct COP is 250/50 = 5; using the Celsius numbers gives −23/50 = −0.46, a negative nonsense value. State that the difference 27 − (−23) survives in either scale, but the numerator must be absolute, so T_C must be 250 K, not −23.

problem: The last sentence contradicts itself. If the vapour leaving the evaporator is superheated, the tail of the evaporator holds superheated vapour, not boiling liquid, so the whole surface cannot stay wet with boiling liquid (that is the flooded-evaporator case, which gives saturated, not superheated, vapour). A student will take away the opposite of the truth.
fix: Replace with: 'Superheat is used with a dry-expansion evaporator, where refrigerant is fed so that it all boils off and the last part of the coil superheats the vapour; a flooded evaporator wets the whole surface but delivers saturated vapour and needs a separate separator to protect the compressor.'

problem: "The same machine, run the other way round, is a heat pump" suggests reversing the machine. A heat pump is the same cycle with the same direction of flow; what changes is the useful output (Q_out instead of Q_in). Students may confuse this with a heat engine run in reverse.
fix: Say: 'The same cycle with a different purpose is a heat pump: it is the condenser heat Q_out, not the evaporator heat Q_in, that we want.'
